questions.question: Q1 What happens to layer thickness when deposition time increases?

explanations.a: Thickness does not decrease with longer deposition.
explanations.c: Correct! Longer deposition time produces thicker films.

questions.question: Q2 If deposition rate doubles while time remains constant, the film thickness will:

explanations.b: Correct! Thickness is directly proportional to deposition rate.

Q5 Which deposition method typically provides excellent surface coverage?

explanations.a: Correct! CVD is known for good conformity and coverage.
explanations.b: PVD coverage is generally lower than CVD.

questions.question: Q6 Which deposition method is commonly used for metal layers?

explanations.a: Correct! PVD is widely used for metal deposition.

questions.question: Q7 Which parameter would most likely increase deposition thickness?

explanations.a: Correct! More deposition time means thicker films.

questions.question: Q8 What is the main purpose of depositing insulating layers?

explanations.a: Correct! Insulating layers separate electrical regions.
explanations.c: Deposition does not affect wafer diameter.

questions.question: Q9 What would happen if deposition continues for too long?

answers.c: The wafer turns into an ingot

explanations.a: Correct! Excessive deposition can create overly thick films.
explanations.c: An ingot is formed during crystal growth.

questions.question: Q10 What is the final outcome of the deposition process?

answers.b: Formation of a thin film layer on the wafer

explanations.b: Correct! Deposition forms thin films on the wafer surface.
explanations.c: Crystal growth is a separate process.
explanations.d: Packaging occurs near the end of fabrication.
